about: Hero devices: what the first screen does and why. Distilled from a study of current motion-led sites, in our own words. A device is a decision, not a template. darkroom deal reads this file.

meanings.material: rare or costly material: the thing itself is the luxury (jewellery, watches, stone, fabric)
meanings.craft: craft and heritage: how it is made, by whom, for how long
meanings.calm: calm and space: time, quiet, nothing asked of you (wellness, private care, retreats)
meanings.precision: precision: engineering, finance, things that must be exact
meanings.status: status and spectacle: the visitor should feel they arrived somewhere, one big moment
meanings.taste: taste and fashion: a point of view, sharp and current
meanings.warmth: warmth and care: people, food, family, neighbourhood
meanings.play: play: the page is fun to touch

sources.material: a material of the subject: a stone, a fabric, foam, rust, wood
sources.place: the place: its street, light, tiles, landscape
sources.time: a time of day or season the subject lives in
sources.product: one colour on the product itself
sources.printed: a printed thing of its world: a ticket, a label, a receipt, a map

devices.name: One object in a void
devices.does: One object on an empty white, grey or black ground. Nothing else competes.
devices.watch: A black object on white has the same drama as a dark hero without a dark page.

devices.name: Object that changes form
devices.does: One object takes a new shape for each message. The story happens without leaving one place.
devices.watch: Each form must mean something, not just look clever.

devices.name: The unveil
devices.does: A cover, sheet, door or fog comes off the subject as the visitor scrolls.
devices.watch: Pay the reveal off with detail shots, not a stock grid.

devices.name: Exploded view
devices.does: The product comes apart so the visitor sees how it is made, then closes again.
devices.watch: Needs a real product with real parts.

devices.name: Whole to detail
devices.does: Starts wide on a person or object and moves in until the material fills the screen.
devices.watch: Works with a few sharp macro photographs if there is no film.

devices.name: One-take journey
devices.does: One continuous camera move through a place, carrying every section.
devices.watch: The place is a journey, never a backdrop.

devices.name: Portal dive
devices.does: The camera passes through a door, lens, eye, keyhole or window into the next world.
devices.watch: The portal should be an object from the subject, not a generic glowing door.

devices.name: Framed window
devices.does: A fixed physical frame holds still while the world inside it changes.
devices.watch: Make the frame belong to the subject: a car windscreen, a shop window.

devices.name: Frosted panel on a bright world
devices.does: Content sits in one soft frosted panel over a real place in daylight. The light version of glass.
devices.watch: Use recipes/liquid-glass.css (.glass--light). One glass material, over something worth blurring.

devices.name: Day as the scroll
devices.does: Scrolling moves the page through dawn, noon, dusk and night, or the seasons.
devices.watch: Good answer for places open all day or work done in shifts.

devices.name: Subject over the word
devices.does: A cut-out subject stands in front of one huge word, so type and picture become one thing.
devices.watch: Needs a clean cut-out and a word that survives being partly hidden.

devices.name: The poster
devices.does: Huge type on one flat colour field. No picture needed.
devices.watch: The strongest option with no assets at all.

devices.name: Drawn as you go
devices.does: Ink, lines or plans draw themselves as the visitor scrolls.
devices.watch: Suits plans, maps, patterns, recipes.

devices.name: One-bit picture
devices.does: The hero is drawn in dither, dots, scanlines or letters, with no colour at all.
devices.watch: Calm software without a gradient.

devices.name: A character that reacts
devices.does: A mascot or character watches the cursor, changes expression or waves.
devices.watch: Personality beats polish, and it was the most-loved type in the study.

devices.name: Pull it, drag it
devices.does: The hero is something the visitor physically moves: stretch, slice, pour, grow.
devices.watch: The verb must belong to the subject.

devices.name: The depth queue
devices.does: Items stand in a receding line, sharp in front and soft behind. The next one steps forward.
devices.watch: Built for lookbooks and shops.

devices.name: The form is the hero
devices.does: One field at a time fills the first screen, so doing the job is the experience.
devices.watch: Only with a real backend; a fake send is a floor rule.

devices.name: The tool is the site
devices.does: The page is a working calculator, atlas, picker or configurator.
devices.watch: Costs the most build time and earns the most trust.

devices.name: Hard cuts
devices.does: No easing: pictures and grounds jump between states like a fashion edit.
devices.watch: A real alternative to every smooth template.

devices.name: Surreal collage
devices.does: Old paintings, cut-outs and one joke. The idea does the work, not the technology.
devices.watch: Use public-domain pictures or generate your own.

devices.name: The page changes colour
devices.does: Each product or option repaints the whole page in its own colour.
devices.watch: Takes a range of products that each own a colour.

devices.name: Tiny world
devices.does: The subject is shown at a wrong scale: tiny workers on a giant object, a whole town on a table.
devices.watch: Friendly and memorable for dull categories.
